ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A certain student cultured Escherichia coli under three conditions ①, ②, and ③. These three conditions are:
① A medium with glucose as the carbon source, continuously supplementing the medium and promptly removing metabolic products
② A medium with glucose as the carbon source, not supplementing the medium and not removing metabolic products
③ A medium with glucose and lactose as the carbon sources, not supplementing the medium and not removing metabolic products
According to the culture results, the trends of the logarithm of the number of bacterial cells changing with time over a period of time are plotted as shown in the figure. Assuming that the initial total sugar amounts in the three media are equal, which trend graphs correspond in order to the three conditions ①②③?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A certain student cultured Escherichia coli under three conditions ①, ②, and ③. These three conditions are: ① A medium with glucose as the carbon source, continuously supplementing the medium and promptly removing metabolic products ② A medium with glucose as the carbon source, not supplementing the medium and not removing metabolic products ③ A medium with glucose and lactose as the carbon sources, not supplementing the medium and not removing metabolic products According to the culture results, the trends of the logarithm of the number of bacterial cells changing with time over a period of time are plotted as shown in the figure. Assuming that the initial total sugar amounts in the three media are equal, which trend graphs correspond in order to the three conditions ①②③?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There are three trend graphs A, B, and C in the figure; the vertical axes are all "logarithmic value of the number of bacterial cells," and the horizontal axes are all "time." The curve in graph A first rises and then tends toward a stable plateau; the curve in graph B first rises, then a period of stagnation or slope change appears in the middle, and then it continues to rise and tends toward a plateau, showing the characteristic of diauxic growth; the curve in graph C continues to rise approximately linearly on the logarithmic coordinate, with no obvious plateau. Then reason: Under condition ①, glucose is used as the carbon source, and the medium is continuously supplemented while metabolic products are promptly removed, so the bacteria can maintain relatively rapid proliferation for a long time; therefore, the logarithm of the number of bacterial cells increases approximately linearly with time, corresponding to C. Under condition ②, there is only glucose and the medium is not supplemented and metabolic products are not removed; nutrients are gradually depleted and metabolic products accumulate, so the bacteria first grow and then enter the stationary phase, corresponding to A. Under condition ③, there are glucose and lactose and there is no supplementation or removal of metabolic products; Escherichia coli preferentially uses glucose, and after glucose is depleted, it needs to induce the lactose metabolism system to use lactose, so a diauxic growth curve appears, corresponding to B. Therefore, ①②③ correspond in order to C, A, B.
